summary: Configured NFS export /srv/nfs/shared on node1 and mounted it at /mnt/shared on node2, both using shared identity dataops (uid/gid 4500) and directory mode 2770 with dataops:dataops ownership. Verified bidirectional file creation preserves consistent ownership/permissions, and root_squash correctly denies root access via NFS (only dataops uid/gid can read/write). Both nodes were then rebooted one at a time (server first, then client), boot-id changes confirmed actual restarts, and post-restart the NFS server, rpcbind, the client's fstab-persisted mount, and read/write access via dataops were all reverified healthy.
actions_performed: Checked OS (RHEL 7.9) and package availability; found no enabled yum repos on either node
Added a temporary CentOS 7 vault-based yum repo and installed nfs-utils/rpcbind on node1 and node2
Created dataops group/user (uid=gid=4500) on node1 and node2
Created /srv/nfs/shared on node1, set ownership dataops:dataops and mode 2770
Configured /etc/exports on node1 scoped to node2's IP with rw,sync,no_subtree_check,root_squash; enabled/started rpcbind and nfs-server; opened firewalld services nfs/rpc-bind/mountd
Created /mnt/shared on node2, added persistent /etc/fstab entry, mounted the NFS share (nfs4)
Verified cross-node file read/write as dataops with correct ownership/mode preserved, and confirmed root_squash denies root-level NFS access as expected
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service status, export table, mount, ownership) on both nodes
Rebooted node1 via shutdown -r now; polled until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id and full recovery of nfs-server/rpcbind/export/directory state
Confirmed node2's live mount and data access survived node1's reboot before proceeding
Rebooted node2 via shutdown -r now; polled until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id and full recovery of the persistent mount, rpcbind, ownership, and dataops read/write access
